segments.title: Reading the opening movements at the River Plate
segments.body: A broad track chart orients the opening of the Battle of the River Plate and gives particular attention to HMS Exeter. Admiral Graf Spee is initially heading toward the British force when the opponents sight one another at about 6 a.m. Their tracks then begin to curve around each other as the action develops. The chart is useful for following the relative movement before gunfire starts, though it is a general outline rather than an exact reconstruction of every ship's course.

evidence.note: The broad action map emphasizes Exeter and shows the opposing forces sighting one another at about 6 a.m.
The map is described as very rough, showing only generalized routes.

segments.summary: A broad battle map shows the ships' movements at first contact and centers HMS Exeter's place in the opening action.

segments.title: Graf Spee opens fire near maximum range
segments.body: The opening action develops quickly, with Admiral Graf Spee firing at about 6:15. The interval after first sighting is uncertain here: the ships might have spotted each other only a minute earlier. Firing at the longest available range is interpreted as an admission of weakness. HMS Exeter has hardly advanced when the shooting begins.

evidence.note: Opening fire is placed at about 6:15, with the suggestion that sighting might have occurred only a minute earlier. The long-range choice is characterized as an admission of weakness.

segments.summary: Graf Spee opens fire near maximum range, a choice interpreted as an admission of weakness in the opening action.

segments.title: Exeter and Ajax reach the killing swing
segments.body: HMS Exeter and HMS Ajax have reached their intended attack position by about 6:50. Admiral Graf Spee has already turned away, with the British cruisers nearly straddling it in the maneuver described as the "killing swing." Exeter has paid heavily for the approach because the German ship concentrated on it as the principal target. The rough battle map shows their relative positions without giving an exact reconstruction of every course.

evidence.note: The discussion of the ships' movements places Exeter and Ajax in their desired killing-swing position around Graf Spee while Exeter has already taken heavy damage as the main target. The map shows generalized routes.

segments.summary: By about 6:50, Exeter and Ajax have reached the desired attack position around Graf Spee, though Exeter has already taken heavy damage as the German ship's main target.

segments.title: Graf Spee underestimates the British cruiser force
segments.body: Admiral Graf Spee had fought a series of relatively easy actions against ships that did not fire back. At the River Plate, the opposing warships returned fire and forced it into a harder fight. German expectations of victory rested on facing a light cruiser and two destroyers. The British force actually comprised a heavy cruiser and two light cruisers, so that assessment understated the opposition.

evidence.note: Graf Spee's earlier opponents had not fired back. The expected British force is described as a light cruiser and two destroyers, followed by the correction that it was a heavy cruiser and two light cruisers.

segments.summary: A mistaken assessment of the British ships helps explain Graf Spee's expectation of victory after earlier actions against merchant shipping.

segments.title: Langsdorff and Harwood fight for different victories
segments.body: For Hans Langsdorff, victory means keeping Admiral Graf Spee afloat and operational. Escape must leave it able to attack more merchant shipping, so merely avoiding sinking would not meet the whole objective. Henry Harwood approaches the fight with the aim of destroying Graf Spee. Those different objectives shape the risks each commander is prepared to accept.

evidence.note: Harwood's aim is to destroy Graf Spee. Langsdorff's definition of victory combines survival, continued operation, and escape to attack more merchant ships.

segments.summary: Langsdorff needs to escape with Graf Spee still able to raid merchant shipping, while Harwood seeks the raider's destruction.
